# epiwave.params 

[![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/acefa-hubs/EpiStrainDynamics/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/acefa-hubs/EpiStrainDynamics)
[![](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-stable-brightgreen.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#stable)
[![Project Status: Active - The project has reached a stable, usable
state and is being actively
developed.](https://www.repostatus.org/badges/latest/active.svg)](https://www.repostatus.org/#active)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/acefa-hubs/EpiStrainDynamics/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/acefa-hubs/EpiStrainDynamics/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)



Delay distributions are manipulated via discrete
#' summation rather than analytic methods. This is justified on two
#' grounds. First, the modelled quantities (case counts, reports) are
#' inherently discrete and observed at daily resolution, making
#' discrete-time convolution the natural representation rather than
#' a numerical approximation of a continuous operation (Cori et al.
#' 2013; Gostic et al. 2020). Second, PMF masses are derived via
#' CDF-differencing — computing mass(d) = CDF(d) - CDF(d-1) — which
#' is the standard approach for discretising continuous delay
#' distributions in infectious disease modelling (Ganyani et al.
#' 2020), and preserves the distributional properties of the
#' underlying continuous distribution within the truncation window.

The goal of epiwave.params a set of general-purpose tools for converting distributional objects and empirical data into PMF representations suitable for discrete-time epidemiological modelling, including convolution.
other tools to manipulate distributions exist but XX has a number of key improvements. 
1. Discretise `distributional` objects to PMF's with quantile-based truncation (parametric_dist_to_distribution)
2. Construct a PMF from empirical data (data_to_distribution)
3. Convert `distributional` objects to a curve for use with serological or similar data (parametric_dist_to_curve)

general-purpose toolbox for the kind of PMF manipulation pipeline 

distcrete (RECON/reconhub) is the closest match to your parametric_dist_to_distribution. It implements a general approach for discretising continuous distributions onto a grid via CDF integration, returning an object with d, p, q, and r functions. CRAN It accepts distribution names as strings and parameters, which covers your parametric_dist_to_distribution use case reasonably well. It is not on CRAN anymore (last updated 2019, archived), is not rOpenSci reviewed, and importantly does not accept distributional objects as input — so your integration with the distributional ecosystem is a genuine differentiator.
actuar::discretize covers the core CDF-differencing step with multiple methods (upper, lower, rounding, unbiased), returning a PMF vector from any CDF function. Rdrr.io It's a lower-level utility without the class structure or distributional integration you have.
epiparameter (Epiverse-Trace, rOpenSci reviewed) is a library of epidemiological parameters with classes for handling delay distributions, including discretisation via a discretise = TRUE argument. Epiverse-trace However its focus is on curating and accessing known literature parameters, not on general-purpose transformation pipelines. It doesn't cover your data_to_distribution or parametric_dist_to_curve use cases.
distr6 supports convolution of distributions analytically, implementing discrete PMF convolution as P(Z=z) = sum_x P(X=x)P(Y=z-x) RDocumentation, but uses R6 classes rather than the distributional/tidyverse-style S3 approach, and doesn't specifically target the epidemiological pipeline context.

## Installation

You can install the development version of epiwave.params from [GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("idem-lab/epiwave.params")
```
